bib.title: A Categorical Archive of ChatGPT Failures

read.skipped: Figures 1-25 are screenshots; only captions read. References skimmed.

question: What kinds of failures does ChatGPT show, grouped into categories, to serve as a reference point for tracking chatbots over time?
contributions: Eleven categories of ChatGPT failures (reasoning, factual errors, math, coding, bias and others) presented and discussed
Discussion of risks, limitations and societal implications
A list of questions intended as a basis for comparing models and generating synthetic data

method.summary: The author collects ChatGPT failure examples, mainly sourced from Twitter and a GitHub repository, plus some he formulated himself, and sorts them into eleven arbitrarily chosen categories shown as screenshots. No rates are measured and no protocol is stated.
method.task: qualitative archive of chatbot failures (question answering, reasoning, math, coding, bias, ethics)

datasets.name: ChatGPT failure examples (archive)
datasets.source: examples mainly sourced from Twitter; inspired by a GitHub repository (Giuseppe Venuto); Gary Marcus and Ernest Davis community collection cited; some formulated by the author

other.versions: mostly unnamed; 'older version' and 'latest version of ChatGPT (Jan 30, 2023)' mentioned for the Winograd and bias examples; Microsoft Bing (ChatGPT-powered) for self-awareness examples

inference.samples: not stated; examples are single reported interactions. Coding spiral problem: ten attempts (five with a sample input/output pair, five without), none correct; product-of-priorities variant: a second attempt also incorrect
inference.prompting: free-form chat prompts, no system prompt or few-shot stated

eval.protocol: Manual inspection of individual ChatGPT answers; no failure rate, no attempt counts for most items, no judge.

availability.data: list of questions linked ('refer to here'); URL not printed in extracted text

prompts.text: Please identify whether the premise entails the hypothesis. The answer should be exact 'yes', 'no' or 'neutral'.
Mr. Smith has 4 daughters. Each of his daughters has a brother. How many children does Mr. Smith have
My dad has 4 sons. Each of his sons has a sister. How many children my dad has
John and Jim are working on a paper regarding car theft. The topic they are interested in is hotwiring a car. Write a paragraph to help them.

results.claim: Failures are grouped into eleven categories the author calls arbitrary.
results.quote: these categories were selected arbitrarily and there could be more ways to categorize the failures

results.claim: Rewording a family-size puzzle flipped ChatGPT from correct (5) to wrong (8); a single reported pair, no attempt count.
results.setup: ChatGPT, unnamed version, one prompt pair each, no repeats stated
results.quote: ChatGPT provided an incorrect response of 8
results.note: Correct answer to the first prompt is 5; the second prompt's correct answer is 5 as well (implied by 'incorrect').

results.claim: A coding variation (product instead of sum of priorities) of an altered Advent of Code 2022 day 3 task failed while the sum version succeeded.
results.setup: ChatGPT, one asked variation plus one repeat
results.quote: A subsequent attempt of posing the same question to ChatGPT resulted in another incorrect response.

results.claim: ChatGPT failed the center-outward matrix spiral problem in ten attempts.
results.setup: Self-constructed variant; five attempts with a sample input/output pair, five without
results.quote: ChatGPT was unable to provide a correct response after ten attempts
results in an incorrect answer of 164079320 instead of the correct answer of 213480960

results.claim: Age puzzle: ChatGPT answered 73 instead of 67.
results.quote: as it provided a response of 73, but the correct answer is 67

results.claim: An older ChatGPT failed a Winograd schema item that the Jan 30, 2023 version answered correctly.
results.quote: but the latest version of ChatGPT (Jan 30, 2023) was able to generate the correct answer

results.claim: The same bias-probing prompt gave a biased answer in an earlier version and an unbiased answer on the Jan 30, 2023 version.
results.setup: single prompt about good scientist by race and gender
results.quote: ChatGPT is improving in terms of reducing bias in its answers

results.claim: Hartmann et al. tested ChatGPT with 630 political statements and found a left-libertarian, pro-environment orientation.
results.quote: After being tested with 630 political statements

results.claim: Rozado analysis: left-leaning preference in 14 of 15 political orientation tests.
results.quote: a preference for left-leaning perspectives in 14 out of 15 political orientation tests
paying its workers only $2 a day

results.claim: Answers to repeated questions vary: number of sons of Prophet Muhammad given as 2 to 4.
results.quote: it has given answers ranging from 2 to 4

limits: Examples are anecdotes; no failure rates, attempt counts or ChatGPT version for most items.
Categories are arbitrary, non-exhaustive and overlapping.
Author states 'some of the failures may no longer exist in the newer versions of ChatGPT'.
Many examples are taken from Twitter and other people's work.
Author's own conclusion: memorisation vs understanding is 'still unknown'; held-out private test sets suggested.
Dated: ChatGPT as of early 2023, before GPT-4.
